item.title: Yuan Still Cheap Versus Euro Even After Gain, Deutsche Bank Says
item.description: China’s yuan is still undervalued versus the euro despite its recent gains, and that’s contributing to a wider European Union trade deficit, according to Deutsche Bank AG.

item.title: SoftBank’s Masayoshi Son Sees Fusion Power as Key to AI’s Future
item.description: SoftBank Group Corp. founder Masayoshi Son said that in the not-so-distant future, nuclear fusion technology will offer the most realistic solution for powering AI data centers’ ballooning needs.

item.title: China’s Crude Oil Imports Plunge to Lowest in Nearly a Decade
item.description: Chinese crude oil imports fell sharply in June to near a decade low, hampered by war in the Persian Gulf and an abrupt slowdown in domestic demand.

item.title: Taiwan Fund Profits 80% After Intervening to Blunt Trump Tariffs
item.description: Taiwan reported a roughly 80% profit from a nine-month-long intervention to support the island’s stock market following the Trump administration’s move to impose tariffs, though it has now exited its position.

item.title: South Korea Turns More Bullish on Economy as Chip Boom Rolls On
item.description: South Korea’s government is taking a more bullish view of the economy than the International Monetary Fund’s recent assessment, maintaining that an artificial intelligence-driven semiconductor boom will continue to outweigh the impact of the Middle East conflict.

item.title: China Exports, Imports Soar Faster Than Forecast as AI Booms
item.description: China’s growth in exports and imports topped all forecasts in June, as surging chip prices and global demand for hardware needed to power AI data centers lift trade across Asia.

item.title: India Large-Caps Eye Comeback on Global Funds’ Support
item.description: Jefferies says large caps are starting to look more reasonably valued.

item.title: Leveraged Chip Bets Backfire in Korea as Biggest ETF Falls 45%
item.description: A new breed of leveraged products tracking major South Korean chip stocks are tumbling in value, threatening steep losses for the country’s retail investors who favor the tools to pursue amplified returns.

item.title: OpenAI’s Feud With xAI Carries On as Apple Secrets Fight Revs Up
item.description: OpenAI asked a judge to find that a lawsuit filed by xAI Corp. accusing the ChatGPT maker of trade secret theft “should never have been filed” and seeks to recoup more than $1 million in legal expenses from Elon Musk’s company.

item.title: China Airline Shares Face More Profit Pain as Demand Stays Weak
item.description: Shares of China’s major airlines are lagging Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd. by nearly 50 percentage points this year, as analysts expect weaker profits to persist on lackluster domestic travel demand.

item.title: SocGen Sees $76 Billion of JGB Buying If GPIF Rebalances Assets
item.description: Japan’s Government Pension Investment Fund has room to buy as much as ¥12.3 trillion ($76 billion) of additional government bonds without changing its asset allocation mix, according to Societe Generale SA, offering potential support for the debt market.

item.title: Phillippine Peso Approaches Record Low as Oil Prices Advance
item.description: The Philippine peso falls toward a record low as escalating tensions in the Middle East drove oil prices higher, putting renewed pressure on the currency.

item.title: Katayama Floats JGBs in Tax-Free Accounts, GPIF Portfolio Review
item.description: Japan’s finance minister floated the idea of adding government bonds to a tax-free investment program for individuals and said the nation’s massive pension fund will adjust its holdings if needed, stepping up efforts to attract cash to domestic markets as the yen trades near 40-year lows.

item.title: SK Hynix Selloff Deepens in Seoul After Wall Street Memory Slump
item.description: SK Hynix Inc. shares fell in Seoul after a rout on Wall Street, reflecting heightened caution among investors following this year’s unprecedented rally in global chipmaker stocks.

item.title: China’s Growth Seen Weakening to Bottom of Official Target Range
item.description: China’s economic growth is expected to have weakened as of the mid-year mark, once again stoking questions about whether policymakers will accelerate government spending to ensure they meet their annual target.

item.title: Australia Consumer, Business Confidence Rise as Fuel Prices Ease
item.description: Australia’s consumer and business confidence improved as concerns about higher fuel prices moderated in response to the US-Iran interim deal, though a resumption in fighting may see this recovery prove short-lived.

item.title: Fed Rate-Hike Bets Mount Before Inflation Data, Warsh Testimony
item.description: Bond traders ramped up bets for a July interest-rate hike ahead of US inflation data and an appearance by the head of the Federal Reserve that stand to reinforce the need for action.

item.title: Singapore’s Economic Growth Slows to 5.7% in Second Quarter
item.description: Singapore’s economy slowed as continued geopolitical tensions in the Middle East tempered the export boost driven by the artificial-intelligence boom.

item.title: Gold Holds Decline on Renewed Hormuz Blockade and Hawkish Fed
item.description: Gold held a decline as escalating hostilities in the Strait of Hormuz and remarks by a US monetary policymaker raised the likelihood of interest-rate hikes to contain inflation.

item.title: RBNZ’s Conway Warns of Sticky Inflation, Risking More Rate Hikes
item.description: New Zealand inflation may not slow as quickly as the Reserve Bank forecasts, Chief Economist Paul Conway said Tuesday, suggesting further interest-rate increases may be in prospect.

item.title: Seidler Equity Is Looking to Sell Stake in 139-Year-Old Baseball Gear Maker Rawlings
item.description: The private equity owner of Rawlings Sporting Goods Co., one of the oldest makers of baseball apparel and equipment, is exploring the sale of its stake in the company in an effort to tap booming investor demand for sports-related investments.

item.title: Brazil’s Oncoclinicas Said to File for Out-of-Court Debt Rework
item.description: Oncoclinicas do Brasil Servicos Medicos SA is preparing to file for an out-of-court debt restructuring, which could come as soon as Monday night, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Huawei's $11 Billion Clean Energy Empire Is Opening New Markets
item.description: Best known for telecoms infrastructure, the Chinese powerhouse has quietly become part of the backbone of the global energy transition.

item.title: Shein’s Slowing Growth Risks Weighing on Hong Kong IPO Valuation
item.description: Shein has finally won long-awaited Chinese regulatory approval for its planned Hong Kong listing, but slowing business growth threatens to weigh on the valuation it can command in the initial public offering.

item.title: UK Industry Tells PM to Move Energy Levies to General Taxation
item.description: High energy costs are undermining the UK’s economic performance, prompting business groups to urge the next government to shift billions of pounds of green levies from electricity bills to general taxation.

item.title: India’s Beaten-Down Large Caps Set to Rebound on Foreign Flows
item.description: India’s large-cap stocks are set to narrow their underperformance to smaller peers, supported by the return of foreign investors, an improving earnings outlook and attractive valuations, according to strategists.

item.title: New Zealand Business Confidence Recovered as Iran War Subsided
item.description: New Zealand business confidence recovered in the second quarter as a tentative US-Iran peace deal helped push down fuel prices, a survey showed.

item.title: Gold Miners Cadillac, Amapa Minerals Add to Canada IPO Rebound
item.description: Cadillac Mines Corp. and Amapa Minerals Holdings Inc. filed for initial public offerings, in the latest sign that the pace of Canadian listings is starting to pick up.

item.title: Oil Holds Gains as Iran Stokes Inflation Worries: Markets Wrap
item.description: Oil held gains and Asian stocks were set to track Wall Street lower after the standoff between the US and Iran intensified, raising concerns that disruptions to energy supplies could accelerate inflation.

item.title: Oil Holds Gains After Trump Reinstates Blockade on Iranian Ships
item.description: Oil steadied after its biggest advance since April, as US President Donald Trump reimposed a blockade on Iranian ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz and demanded payment for all other cargo moving through the waterway.
